title: Infectious mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes are reactive CD8+ T cells
vignette: A 15-year-old girl is evaluated due to persistent fever, fatigue, and sore throat. Physical examination reveals splenomegaly and symmetric posterior cervical lymphadenopathy. A peripheral blood smear shows large, atypical lymphocytes with abundant basophilic cytoplasm and a cell membrane that conforms to the borders of neighboring red cells. The atypical cells seen here are most likely an activated form of which of the following?

clues.text: persistent fever, fatigue, and sore throat
clues.note: Fever, fatigue, and pharyngitis in an adolescent are classic for infectious mononucleosis (Epstein-Barr virus).

clues.text: splenomegaly and symmetric posterior cervical lymphadenopathy
clues.note: Splenomegaly with POSTERIOR cervical lymphadenopathy is characteristic of infectious mononucleosis.

clues.text: large, atypical lymphocytes with abundant basophilic cytoplasm
clues.note: Atypical (reactive) lymphocytes - large, with abundant basophilic cytoplasm molding around neighboring cells - are the reactive CD8+ T cells responding to EBV.

whatMatters: Fever + pharyngitis + posterior cervical adenopathy + splenomegaly + ATYPICAL LYMPHOCYTES = infectious mononucleosis (EBV). EBV infects B cells (via CD21), but the atypical lymphocytes on the smear are reactive/activated CD8+ CYTOTOXIC T LYMPHOCYTES mounting the antiviral response. Answer B.
strategy: Distinguish the infected cell from the reactive cell: EBV INFECTS B lymphocytes (CD21 receptor), but the ATYPICAL lymphocytes seen on the smear are the host's reactive CD8+ T cells (>95% of atypical cells). Pick CD8+ cytotoxic lymphocytes. Reject CD4+ helper cells and CD21+ B cells (the infected cells, a minority of atypical cells), monocytes (vacuolated grayish cytoplasm, not this), and plasma cells (eccentric nucleus, perinuclear hof).

eliminations.label: CD4+ helper lymphocytes - minority of atypical cells
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: CD4 helper T cells. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: activated CD4 cells can look similar, but the atypical lymphocytes in mononucleosis are predominantly CD8+ cytotoxic T cells (>95%). ✅ Correct if: asking about helper T-cell responses generally.

eliminations.label: CD14+ monocytes - different morphology (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: monocytes (CD14). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: monocytosis can occur in chronic infection, but monocytes have vacuolated, grayish cytoplasm - not the basophilic reactive lymphocyte molding seen here. ✅ Correct if: a monocyte-predominant process.

eliminations.label: CD21+ lymphocytes - the INFECTED B cells (not the atypical cells)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: B lymphocytes, which EBV infects via the CD21 receptor. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: B cells are the cells that are INFECTED, but they make up <5% of the atypical lymphocytes; the reactive atypical cells are CD8+ T cells. ✅ Correct if: asking which cell EBV directly infects (CD21+ B cells).

eliminations.label: CD27+ plasma cells - eccentric nucleus/hof
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: activated plasma cells (ovoid, eccentric nucleus, perinuclear clearing/spoke-wheel chromatin). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that is a different morphology and not the reactive T cells of mononucleosis. ✅ Correct if: identifying a plasma cell.

reasoning: Adolescent with fever, pharyngitis, posterior cervical adenopathy, splenomegaly, and atypical lymphocytes = infectious mononucleosis (EBV)
EBV infects B cells (CD21), but the atypical lymphocytes are the host's antiviral response
These reactive/atypical cells are predominantly CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes
mechanism: Infectious mononucleosis is caused by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), which enters through the pharyngeal mucosa and preferentially INFECTS B LYMPHOCYTES by binding the CD21 receptor. Infected B cells present viral antigens on MHC class I, triggering a vigorous host response by REACTIVE (ATYPICAL) CD8+ CYTOTOXIC T LYMPHOCYTES that clonally expand to destroy virus-infected cells. These reactive CD8+ T cells are what appear on the peripheral smear as ATYPICAL LYMPHOCYTES - larger than resting lymphocytes, with abundant basophilic cytoplasm and a membrane that molds ('conforms') around adjacent red cells (Downey cells); they make up >10% of lymphocytes, and >95% are CD8+ T cells. Clinically, mononucleosis presents with fever, exudative pharyngitis, fatigue, posterior cervical (or generalized) lymphadenopathy, and splenomegaly (avoid contact sports due to rupture risk); the heterophile (Monospot) antibody test is positive. Thus the atypical cells are activated CD8+ T cells, not the infected CD21+ B cells (a small minority), CD4 cells, monocytes, or plasma cells.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro/Heme > infectious mononucleosis (EBV): infects B cells (CD21); atypical lymphocytes = reactive CD8+ T cells (>95%); fever, posterior cervical adenopathy, splenomegaly; positive heterophile (Monospot).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: EBV infects B cells, but the atypical smear cells are reactive CD8+ cytotoxic T cells.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on atypical/reactive lymphocyte, CD8 vs CD4, CD21 (EBV receptor), Downey cells, or heterophile antibody? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: CD21+ B cells are the INFECTED cells (minority of atypical cells); CD4/monocytes/plasma cells are wrong lineages/morphology.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the smear: a large lymphocyte with abundant basophilic cytoplasm that indents around neighboring red cells (atypical/reactive lymphocyte). Anchor: 'atypical lymphocyte in mono = reactive CD8+ T cell.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: EBV mono - infects B cells (CD21), atypical cells = reactive CD8+ T cells; posterior cervical adenopathy + splenomegaly; Monospot positive.

keywords.back: Fever, pharyngitis, posterior cervical adenopathy, splenomegaly

Immuno > CD4 (helper), CD8 (cytotoxic), CD21 (B cell/EBV), CD14 (monocyte).

memoryHook: EBV hides in B cells, but the smear's big blue atypical lymphocytes are the CD8 T-cell posse hunting them - the reactive cells, not the infected ones.
